this is the spec the office sent for the weekly file. the reader has to follow it exactly, I'll ask about bits of it as we go.

SKERRY HARBOUR OFFICE
Weekly Catch File, format version 4
Issued by the harbour office, revised for the spring season

1. Purpose
Every boat that lands at this harbour hands in one catch file per calendar week. The office reads the files to check landings against each licence and to report the totals to the district. A file that does not follow this document is returned to the skipper unread, so the layout below is exact, not a guide.

2. File naming
A file is named year, a dash, the letter W, the two digit week number, a dash, then the boat name in lower case with single dashes between words, and the ending .csv. Example: 2026-W09-kittiwake.csv. Weeks run Monday to Sunday and week 01 is the week that holds the first Thursday of the year.

3. Header record
The first line of the file is the header record. It holds six values separated by commas, in this order, with no spaces around the commas.
  version  whole number  Must be 4 for this format. Older units still send 3 and are rejected.
  boat     whole number  The harbour boat number, 1 to 999, no leading zeros.
  licence  text          The letter L, a dash, then four digits.
  week     text          Year, dash, W and week number as in the file name.
  unit     text          kg or lb. Applies to every weight in the file.
  count    whole number  The number of catch records that follow. A mismatch is an error.

4. Catch record
Each line after the header is one catch record with nine values.
  day      date      Day of landing as year-month-day. Must fall inside the week named in the header.
  port     text      Four character port code from section 6.
  species  text      Three character species code from section 5.
  gear     text      One of pots, trawl, nets, lines, dredge, creels.
  weight   decimal   Landed weight in the unit from the header. One decimal place at most. Never negative.
  grade    whole number1 for prime, 2 for standard, 3 for under size. Under size is landed but not counted against quota.
  hours    decimal   Hours fished for this record.
  crew     whole numberCrew aboard, 1 to 9.
  note     text      Free text, up to 60 characters, may be empty. Commas are not allowed.

5. Species codes
Code, species, minimum landing size in centimetres where one applies.

7. Rules of validity
  7.1  A file whose header count does not match the number of catch records is rejected as a whole.
  7.2  A day outside the week named in the header makes that one record invalid.
  7.3  A weight of zero is allowed only when the note says why, for example gear lost.
  7.4  The same species, port, gear and day may appear on more than one line. The lines are added together.
  7.5  Weights over 5000 in kg, or over 11000 in lb, are queried by the office before they are accepted.
  7.6  A record with grade 3 is stored but never counted towards the weekly limit.
  7.7  Hours fished above 168 for one record are impossible and invalid.
  7.8  Crew above 9 or below 1 is invalid.
  7.9  A file with no catch records is valid and means the boat did not fish that week.
  7.10  Blank lines at the end of the file are ignored. A blank line in the middle is an error.
  7.11  A species code that is not in section 5 makes that record invalid, whatever the spelling.
  7.12  A port code that is not in section 6 makes that record invalid.
  7.13  Commas inside the note are not allowed, even inside quote marks. Quote marks are not used in this format.
  7.14  The licence in the header must match the licence the office holds for the boat number.
  7.15  Two files for the same boat and week are a duplicate. The later one, by the date the office received it, replaces the earlier.
  7.16  A file may not mix kg and lb. If a skipper changes unit mid week, two files are handed in and the second one is marked as a correction in the note of its first record.

9. Changes from version 3
  1. The header gained the count value.
  2. Grade 3 records no longer count towards the limit.
  3. Port codes grew from three characters to four.
  4. The note value is now limited to 60 characters.
  5. Quote marks were removed from the format altogether.
